text.title: Java Spring Boot Enterprise Patterns Failure Modes
text.summary: 8 antipatterns observed in real enterprise Spring Boot 3 codebases. Each pairs symptom + root cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Adding an entity to `HashSet` triggers infinite recursion; `equals` walks lazy collections and loads them.
antipattern.root-cause: Author put `@Data` on a JPA entity; generated `equals` / `hashCode` traverse all fields.
antipattern.fix: Use `@Getter @Setter` only; implement `equals`/`hashCode` over a business key on top of `BaseEntity.id`.

antipattern.symptom: List endpoint executes 1 + N queries per row; profile shows N additional `SELECT` per page.
antipattern.root-cause: Mapper or controller accesses a lazy association after the transaction closes.
antipattern.fix: Project to DTO inside the service `@Transactional` boundary; use `@EntityGraph` / `JOIN FETCH`. Add `n-plus-one-assertion.java` test that asserts a max query count.

antipattern.symptom: Concurrent edits silently overwrite each other; audit trail shows lost updates with no exception.
antipattern.root-cause: Entity did not extend `BaseEntity`; `@Version` field missing; last-write-wins.
antipattern.fix: Inherit `BaseEntity`; catch `OptimisticLockException` in the service and surface 409 via `ProblemDetail`.

antipattern.symptom: Each controller returns a different JSON error shape; clients implement N different parsers. Where no handler exists at all, the production 500 carries Spring's default body including a stack trace.
antipattern.root-cause: No `@RestControllerAdvice`; each controller invents its own, and unhandled exceptions fall through to the default error attributes.
antipattern.fix: Add one `@RestControllerAdvice` extending `ResponseEntityExceptionHandler`, mapping every domain exception → `ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(...)` with a stable `type` URI. Delete per-controller `try/catch` for cross-cutting handling.

antipattern.symptom: Read-heavy endpoint runs slow under load; Hibernate flushes the dirty-check cache on every method exit.
antipattern.root-cause: Service has no class-level `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`; every method opens a writable transaction.
antipattern.fix: Add `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` at class level; override on write methods. Verify with a single integration test that read endpoints log zero `UPDATE` statements.

antipattern.symptom: A bean carries 15 `@Value("${...}")` fields. Renaming a property in `application.yml` breaks code the compiler never touched, and the failure appears at runtime.
antipattern.root-cause: String-based property access spread bean by bean, with no central type-safe binding.
antipattern.fix: Collapse each concern into one `@ConfigurationProperties` record (`MailProperties`, `AuthProperties`) and inject the record per `config-properties-typed`.

antipattern.symptom: The deploy reports success; the first request that touches the retry path fails with `NumberFormatException` because `retry.delay=abc`.
antipattern.root-cause: The property was bound by `@Value` at injection time with no validation, so the bad value reached business logic unchecked.
antipattern.fix: Bind via `@ConfigurationProperties` + `@Validated` per `config-validation-on-properties`, so the misconfiguration fails context startup with a `ConstraintViolation` naming the property.

antipattern.symptom: `if (env.equals("prod")) sendEmail(); else log(...);` — after a refactor, development starts sending real email to real customers.
antipattern.root-cause: Environment branching decided at runtime instead of at bean-wiring time.
antipattern.fix: Replace the branch with two beans — `@Profile("prod") EmailSender realSender()` and `@Profile("!prod") EmailSender logSender()` — or `@ConditionalOnProperty` for a feature flag, per `config-conditional-on-property`.
